action: Give school-implementable recommendations
wording: The {role} should give the school recommendations for {preferredName} that can be implemented in an ordinary classroom by ordinary staff, naming who does what and how often, and review them with the school at least annually with family consent, so advice is usable rather than aspirational.
frequency: at each report and reviewed at least annually
intensity: Written recommendations with named roles and frequencies
evidence_to_monitor: recommendations implemented; recommendations that could not be implemented and why

action: Observe in the real setting before advising
wording: The {role} should observe {preferredName} in the actual classroom or setting before finalising recommendations, and adjust them to what the environment allows, so the advice fits the school {preferredName} attends.
frequency: at least once before each set of recommendations
intensity: In-setting observation followed by revised written advice
evidence_to_monitor: what the observation changed in the advice

action: Train and monitor the staff implementing the technique
wording: The {role} should train the school staff who implement any prescribed technique, programme or equipment for {preferredName}, observe them doing it, and review it at an agreed interval, so the technique is delivered as intended and safely.
frequency: initial training, observation within the first month, then reviewed each semester
intensity: Hands-on training with observation and sign-off
evidence_to_monitor: staff trained and observed; fidelity to the technique
linked_activities: Undertaking Tasks Independently; Positioning One’s Body

action: Co-write the behaviour support plan
wording: The {role} should write {preferredName}'s behaviour support plan with {preferredName}, the family and the teaching team, naming the triggers, the early signs, the agreed response and who does what, so every adult responds the same way rather than to their own judgement in the moment.
frequency: written once and reviewed each term or after any significant incident
intensity: Documented plan with named responders, known to everyone who teaches the student
evidence_to_monitor: how closely the agreed response was followed; incidents and their triggers

action: Coach staff in the agreed response
wording: The {role} should coach {preferredName}'s teachers in the agreed response and de-escalation approach, observe it in practice and give feedback, so the plan is used as written rather than as each adult remembers it.
frequency: initial coaching, then observation and feedback once a term
intensity: Modelling, observation and feedback with the staff involved
evidence_to_monitor: consistency of response across staff; escalation frequency

action: Review the incident pattern, not just the incident
wording: The {role} should review {preferredName}'s incident records at least fortnightly, looking for patterns of time, subject, setting or person, and change the plan where a pattern is clear, so the response addresses the cause rather than repeating the consequence.
frequency: at least fortnightly
intensity: Pattern analysis with documented changes to the plan
evidence_to_monitor: patterns identified; changes made and their effect

action: Check consequences against the plan
wording: The {role} should check any consequence, suspension or referral proposed for {preferredName} against the plan and the identified disability-related need before it is applied, so a response to disability-related behaviour is not treated as a simple choice.
frequency: before any consequence or referral is applied
intensity: Plan checked and the decision recorded with its reasoning
evidence_to_monitor: consequences applied and their consistency with the plan

action: Raise implementation barriers rather than dropping the adjustment
wording: The {role} should raise with the plan coordinator any adjustment for {preferredName} that cannot be implemented as written, within a fortnight of the problem appearing, so it is redesigned rather than quietly dropped.
frequency: within a fortnight of any implementation problem
intensity: Direct written or verbal notification with the specific barrier named
evidence_to_monitor: barriers raised and what was agreed instead

action: Bring specific evidence to the review
wording: The {role} should bring specific evidence to each review of {preferredName}'s plan — what was tried, what happened, work samples and the level of support needed — rather than a general impression, so decisions rest on classroom reality.
frequency: before each review meeting
intensity: Short written evidence per adjustment, with work samples where relevant
evidence_to_monitor: evidence supplied per adjustment; decisions changed by it

action: Brief the relief teacher before a planned absence
wording: The {role} should leave the class summary of {preferredName}'s adjustments for any relief teacher before a planned absence, including what to do if things are difficult, so a day with a different teacher is not a day without adjustments.
frequency: before every planned absence
intensity: Written summary left with the lesson plan
evidence_to_monitor: days with relief staff and how they went

action: Keep teaching and quality first teaching in place
wording: The {role} should continue to teach, assess and plan for {preferredName} alongside any targeted or intensive support, keeping responsibility for {preferredName}'s learning rather than transferring it to the support staff working with them.
frequency: every lesson
intensity: Teacher-led planning, teaching and assessment continues at every level of support
evidence_to_monitor: teacher-set goals and progress against them; who directs the support in the room

action: Make sure identity is part of the plan
wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s cultural identity, language and community connections are reflected in the plan, with the family's consent about what is recorded, so support is built on who {preferredName} is rather than only on what is difficult.
frequency: at each plan review
intensity: Family-led contribution recorded in the plan with consent
evidence_to_monitor: what the family and student identify as important; adjustments changed as a result
linked_activities: Responding to the Feelings of Others

action: Make meetings work for the family
wording: The {role} should arrange {preferredName}'s meetings so the family can take part — timing, location, interpreters, who attends and how the meeting is run — and check with the family afterwards that it worked, so participation is real rather than formal.
frequency: before and after each meeting
intensity: Arrangements agreed with the family in advance and checked afterwards
evidence_to_monitor: family attendance and participation; what the family asks to change

action: Brief staff on culturally responsive practice
wording: The {role} should brief the staff working with {preferredName} on the culturally responsive practice agreed with the family, including what to avoid, before those staff first work with {preferredName}, so cultural safety does not depend on individual awareness.
frequency: before first contact and at the start of each year
intensity: Briefing with the agreed practice written down
evidence_to_monitor: staff practice reported by the student and family
linked_activities: Interacting According to Social Rules; Interpreting Non-Verbal Messages

action: Connect the student with community and mentoring
wording: The {role} should connect {preferredName} with cultural mentoring or community programmes the family agrees to, and follow up that the connection was made, so the school is not the only source of support.
frequency: at least once a semester, with follow-up within a month
intensity: Referral plus follow-up confirming contact
evidence_to_monitor: connections made and sustained; student's engagement with them

action: Keep cover consistent for this student
wording: The {role} should keep cover for {preferredName}'s classes as consistent as possible, using the same relief teachers where there is a choice, so an absent teacher does not also mean an unfamiliar adult every time.
frequency: each time a class is covered
intensity: Same relief staff used where a choice exists
evidence_to_monitor: how often a familiar adult covered the class

action: Get the summary to the relief teacher
wording: The {role} should make sure the relief teacher receives {preferredName}'s one-page summary of adjustments before the lesson starts, so a covered lesson is not a lesson without adjustments.
frequency: before every covered lesson
intensity: Summary supplied with the cover notes as a matter of routine
evidence_to_monitor: covered lessons where the summary was supplied; how those lessons went

action: Protect timetabled support staffing
wording: The {role} should keep {preferredName}'s timetabled support staffing in place rather than redeploying it to cover elsewhere, and tell the plan owner the same day when it genuinely cannot be held, so the loss is visible rather than silent.
frequency: each day support is timetabled
intensity: Allocation protected, with same-day notification when it cannot be
evidence_to_monitor: days the agreed support was not available and why

action: Convene and document the student support group
wording: The {role} should convene and document a student support group meeting for {preferredName} each term, recording the agreed adjustments, who is responsible for each one and the review date, and sharing that record with every teacher who teaches {preferredName}, so the same adjustments are implemented across every class rather than in some of them.
frequency: once each term, and after any significant change
intensity: Planned meeting with documented actions and named owners
evidence_to_monitor: adjustments agreed and who owns each one; actions completed between meetings; what teachers report is working

action: Keep the record of adjustments current
wording: The {role} should keep {preferredName}'s record of adjustments current, updating it whenever an adjustment is added, changed or faded, and checking the written record against what is actually happening in classes at least once a term, so the documented plan and {preferredName}'s daily experience describe the same thing.
frequency: updated as changes occur, checked against practice each term
intensity: Record maintained by one named person, cross-checked with teachers
evidence_to_monitor: date and reason for each change; gaps found between the record and practice

action: Brief new and relieving staff before they teach the student
wording: The {role} should brief every new teacher, casual relief teacher and support staff member before they work with {preferredName}, using a one-page summary of the agreed adjustments and what to do if things go wrong, so support does not drop away when staffing changes.
frequency: before the first lesson with any new or relieving staff member
intensity: Short verbal briefing plus a written one-page summary
evidence_to_monitor: who was briefed and when; whether adjustments continued during the staffing change

action: Gather evidence across the year, not the week before
wording: The {role} should collect evidence for {preferredName}'s plan and any funding or profile process across the whole year — teacher observations, work samples, specialist reports, student voice and family voice — rather than in the fortnight beforehand, so the picture presented is an accurate description of a normal school week.
frequency: ongoing, with a collection point each term
intensity: Structured collection against each functional area, held in one place
evidence_to_monitor: range and dates of evidence held; functional areas with thin evidence

action: Review each term what can be faded
wording: The {role} should review with {preferredName}'s teachers each term which adjustments are still needed, which should increase and which can be faded, so the level of adult support matches current evidence rather than what was agreed a year ago.
frequency: once each term
intensity: Structured review of each adjustment against recent evidence
evidence_to_monitor: adjustments faded and what happened next; adjustments increased and why

action: Timetable the agreed support before the term starts
wording: The {role} should arrange and timetable the agreed additional support for {preferredName} — staffing, spaces and equipment — before the term begins and confirm it with each teacher, so the adjustment is available from the first lesson instead of being negotiated week by week.
frequency: before the start of each term and after any timetable change
intensity: Confirmed allocation in writing before the term starts
evidence_to_monitor: lessons where the agreed support was not available and why

action: Escalate unresolved implementation barriers
wording: The {role} should escalate to the principal class any barrier that stops an agreed adjustment being implemented for {preferredName} and that has not been resolved within a fortnight of being raised, so problems are dealt with at the level that can actually fix them.
frequency: whenever a barrier remains unresolved after a fortnight
intensity: Written escalation naming the barrier and what is needed
evidence_to_monitor: barriers raised, resolved and outstanding

action: Translate specialist advice into school actions
wording: The {role} should meet with the specialists involved with {preferredName}, with family consent, and translate their recommendations into specific school actions with a named owner and a start date, so advice becomes practice rather than a report in a file.
frequency: after each new report and at least once a year
intensity: Documented conversion of each recommendation into an owned action
evidence_to_monitor: recommendations received and the action taken for each

action: Keep the agreed response available
wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s agreed first aid response, medication and equipment are available and in date at all times the school operates, including sport and offsite activities, so the response does not depend on where {preferredName} is that day.
frequency: checked at the start of each term and before each offsite activity
intensity: Stock, currency and location checked against the plan
evidence_to_monitor: checks completed; occasions the response was needed and what was available

action: Record and pass on every event
wording: The {role} should record every first aid event involving {preferredName} and pass it to the health plan owner and the family the same day, so a pattern is noticed early rather than at the end of term.
frequency: same day, every time
intensity: Written record shared with the plan owner and family
evidence_to_monitor: events recorded; patterns identified

action: Brief the staff on duty
wording: The {role} should brief the staff on yard and sport duty on {preferredName}'s signs and the required response, at the start of each term and whenever the duty roster changes, so the right response is available wherever {preferredName} is.
frequency: at the start of each term and on roster changes
intensity: Briefing plus a response card carried by duty staff
evidence_to_monitor: staff briefed; accuracy of the response given

action: Put the universal practices in place first
wording: The {role} should make sure the practices that reduce the need for individual adjustment — predictable routines, accessible materials, clear instructions, known expectations — are in place across the school, so individual adjustments are reserved for what universal practice cannot cover.
frequency: reviewed each semester as part of school planning
intensity: Whole-school practice, monitored and supported rather than assumed
evidence_to_monitor: consistency across classes; individual adjustments no longer needed once universal practice improved

action: Look at patterns across students, not just this one
wording: The {role} should look for patterns across the students on plans — the same barrier appearing in the same subject, setting or time of day — and report them to leadership each semester, so recurring problems are fixed once rather than student by student.
frequency: each semester
intensity: Cross-cohort analysis with a written report to leadership
evidence_to_monitor: patterns identified and the whole-school change made

action: Run professional learning on the adjustments in use
wording: The {role} should run professional learning for staff on the adjustments actually in use in the school, with practice and follow-up rather than a single session, so staff can implement them confidently.
frequency: at least once a semester with follow-up in teams
intensity: Sessions with modelling, practice and follow-up support
evidence_to_monitor: staff confidence; implementation observed after the learning

action: Build the literacy adjustment into unit planning
wording: The {role} should work with {preferredName}'s teachers at the start of each unit to build the agreed literacy adjustment into the unit's texts, tasks and assessments, so the adjustment is part of the planned work rather than something added when {preferredName} struggles.
frequency: at the start of each unit
intensity: Planning conversation per unit with the adjustment written into the plan
evidence_to_monitor: adjustment named in unit planning; student access to the unit's texts

action: Set the reading demand of materials
wording: The {role} should check the reading demand of the materials {preferredName} is given and supply an accessible version at the agreed reading level, keeping the same learning goal, so reading load is not the reason {preferredName} cannot show what they know.
frequency: for each unit and before each assessment
intensity: Materials checked and adapted in advance, learning goal unchanged
evidence_to_monitor: reading level of materials provided; tasks completed independently

action: Model the literacy strategy in class
wording: The {role} should model the agreed explicit literacy strategy in {preferredName}'s classes and coach the teacher to continue it, so the strategy is used consistently rather than only when a specialist is present.
frequency: at least once per teacher, then follow-up coaching each term
intensity: In-class modelling followed by teacher-led practice and feedback
evidence_to_monitor: strategy in use across classes; student response to the strategy

action: Coordinate targeted literacy intervention
wording: The {role} should coordinate a targeted literacy intervention for {preferredName} at an agreed frequency, with an entry point set from assessment data and progress checked at a set interval, so the intervention is adjusted on evidence rather than continued out of habit.
frequency: sessions at the agreed frequency, progress checked every five weeks
intensity: Small-group or individual instruction with documented entry point and progress checks
evidence_to_monitor: progress against the entry point; transfer of the skill into class work

action: Short-term goal-focused individual sessions
wording: The {role} should provide short-term, goal-focused individual sessions with {preferredName} at an agreed frequency, with the goals and a review point written down at the start, so support is purposeful and its effect can be judged.
frequency: an agreed number of sessions, commonly weekly, with a review point
intensity: Individual sessions with documented goals and a planned end or review
evidence_to_monitor: progress against the agreed goals; student view of the sessions
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Turn session work into classroom strategies
wording: The {role} should give {preferredName}'s teachers two or three specific, practical classroom strategies drawn from the sessions, with {preferredName}'s consent about what is shared, so the same approach is used in class and in the session.
frequency: at the start of the support and after each review point
intensity: Brief written strategies plus a conversation with the teaching team
evidence_to_monitor: strategies used in class and their effect
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Contribute to the safety or support plan
wording: The {role} should contribute to {preferredName}'s safety or support plan where a risk has been identified, setting out the warning signs, the agreed response and who does what, and review it after any incident, so staff respond consistently rather than improvising.
frequency: at plan development, then reviewed each term and after any incident
intensity: Documented plan with named responders and review points
evidence_to_monitor: warning signs observed; how closely the agreed response was followed
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Warm handover to an external service
wording: The {role} should make a warm handover to any external service {preferredName} is referred to, with family consent, and follow up within a fortnight to confirm contact was made, so a referral does not end at the point of paperwork.
frequency: at referral, with follow-up within a fortnight
intensity: Direct contact between practitioners plus follow-up confirmation
evidence_to_monitor: referrals made and whether contact was established
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Coach staff in the agreed regulation approach
wording: The {role} should coach the staff who work with {preferredName} in the agreed co-regulation and de-escalation approach, modelling it and observing it in practice, so the approach is used the same way by everyone rather than differently in each class.
frequency: initial coaching, then observation and feedback once a term
intensity: Modelling, observation and feedback with the staff involved
evidence_to_monitor: consistency of the response across staff; escalation frequency
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Build the numeracy adjustment into unit planning
wording: The {role} should work with {preferredName}'s mathematics teachers at the start of each unit to build the agreed numeracy adjustment into the tasks and assessments, so access is planned rather than improvised in the lesson.
frequency: at the start of each unit
intensity: Planning conversation per unit with the adjustment written into the plan
evidence_to_monitor: adjustment named in unit planning; access to the unit's tasks

action: Provide the agreed tools and scaffolds
wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName} has the agreed numeracy tools and scaffolds — concrete materials, a calculator, formula or steps reference — available in every relevant lesson, so working memory and recall are not what limits the mathematics {preferredName} can do.
frequency: in every relevant lesson
intensity: Tools available by default, without the student having to ask
evidence_to_monitor: tools used and by whose prompt; tasks attempted and completed

action: Set the entry point from data
wording: The {role} should use {preferredName}'s numeracy assessment data to set the point the teaching starts from, and share that with the teachers, so tasks sit where {preferredName} can actually work rather than at the year level by default.
frequency: at the start of each year and after each assessment cycle
intensity: Data analysis translated into a stated entry point per teacher
evidence_to_monitor: growth from the entry point; match between tasks set and the entry point

action: Coordinate targeted numeracy intervention
wording: The {role} should coordinate a targeted numeracy intervention for {preferredName} at an agreed frequency, checking progress at a set interval and stopping or changing it if the evidence does not show growth, so time out of class is justified by what it produces.
frequency: sessions at the agreed frequency, progress checked every five weeks
intensity: Small-group or individual instruction with documented progress checks
evidence_to_monitor: progress against the entry point; transfer into class work

action: Maintain and review the health support plan
wording: The {role} should maintain {preferredName}'s health support plan with the family and the treating practitioner, train the staff named in it, and review it at least annually and after any health event, so the school response is current and delivered by trained people.
frequency: reviewed annually and after any health event
intensity: Written plan, named trained staff, training currency tracked
evidence_to_monitor: training currency; health events and the response given

action: Make sure the health procedure travels with the student
wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s medication, equipment and health procedure are available wherever the school programme takes place, including excursions, camps and sport, so participation is never limited by where the equipment is kept.
frequency: before every offsite activity and daily on site
intensity: Checked against the plan before each activity
evidence_to_monitor: activities attended; occasions the procedure was needed offsite

action: Brief staff on signs and the required response
wording: The {role} should brief the staff who teach or supervise {preferredName} on the signs to watch for and the exact response required, before those staff first work with {preferredName} and again each year, so the response does not depend on who happens to be there.
frequency: before first contact and annually
intensity: Briefing plus a written response card held where staff can reach it
evidence_to_monitor: staff briefed and when; accuracy of the response given

action: Review after any health incident
wording: The {role} should review the plan with the family after any health incident involving {preferredName}, within a week, and change the plan where the incident showed it was needed, so the plan improves each time it is tested.
frequency: within a week of any health incident
intensity: Documented review with the family and changes made to the plan
evidence_to_monitor: incidents and the plan changes that followed

action: Resource the agreed adjustments
wording: The {role} should make sure the adjustments agreed for {preferredName} are resourced — staffing, time, spaces and equipment — and named in the school's planning, so implementation does not depend on the goodwill of individual staff.
frequency: at each planning and budget cycle, and when needs change
intensity: Allocation confirmed in the school's own planning documents
evidence_to_monitor: adjustments that could not be delivered for resourcing reasons

action: Approve and time-limit any reduction in access
wording: The {role} should approve, document and review any arrangement that reduces {preferredName}'s access to the full timetable or programme, setting a review date and a written plan for returning to full access, so a short-term measure does not quietly become permanent.
frequency: at the point of the decision, then reviewed at least every four weeks
intensity: Written approval, named review date, plan to restore full access
evidence_to_monitor: hours of programme accessed; progress against the return plan

action: Meet the family at leadership level
wording: The {role} should meet {preferredName}'s family at agreed points across the year, and whenever the family raises an unresolved concern, so concerns are heard by someone who can act on them and the relationship does not rest on one staff member.
frequency: at least once a semester and whenever a concern is unresolved
intensity: Direct leadership contact with agreed follow-up actions
evidence_to_monitor: concerns raised and how each was resolved

action: Approve and review safety-critical arrangements
wording: The {role} should approve the risk assessment and duty-of-care arrangements for any safety-critical adjustment for {preferredName}, confirm the staff involved are trained, and review the arrangement after any incident, so safety does not depend on informal practice.
frequency: before the arrangement starts, then reviewed each term and after any incident
intensity: Documented approval, named trained staff, incident review
evidence_to_monitor: training currency; incidents and the review outcome

action: Build the adjustments into staff professional learning
wording: The {role} should include the practices {preferredName} depends on in whole-staff professional learning and planning, so the adjustment is part of how the school teaches rather than an exception a few staff know about.
frequency: at least once a year in the professional learning schedule
intensity: Scheduled whole-staff learning with follow-up in teams
evidence_to_monitor: staff confidence and consistency reported by teachers

action: Protect the plan through staffing and year-level changes
wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s plan and adjustments are handed over whenever the teaching team, year level or leadership changes, with the handover completed before the change takes effect, so nothing has to be rebuilt from scratch.
frequency: before every staffing, year level or leadership change
intensity: Documented handover with the receiving staff named
evidence_to_monitor: handovers completed on time; adjustments lost after a change

action: Teach the specific skill explicitly
wording: The {role} should teach {preferredName} the specific self-management or social skill named in the plan explicitly, at an agreed time each week, and tell the teachers which skill to reinforce that fortnight, so the skill is taught rather than expected.
frequency: one session a week, with the reinforcement focus shared each fortnight
intensity: Explicit teaching with a named focus reinforced in class
evidence_to_monitor: the skill in use outside the session; student's own account of what is getting easier

action: Put the capability goal in the curriculum plan
wording: The {role} should make sure {preferredName}'s personal and social capability goal appears in the curriculum plan and in reporting alongside academic goals, so growth in these areas is recognised as learning rather than as behaviour.
frequency: at each planning and reporting cycle
intensity: Goal written into planning and reported on
evidence_to_monitor: progress reported against the capability goal

action: Set up a structured social opportunity
wording: The {role} should set up a structured activity at break times that {preferredName} can join with a known adult nearby, and step that adult back as {preferredName} settles, so social contact is available without depending on an adult being present.
frequency: at the agreed break times each week
intensity: Structured activity with adult support that reduces over time
evidence_to_monitor: participation; time spent without adult support

action: Co-design the regulation strategies with the student
wording: The {role} should design {preferredName}'s self-regulation strategies with {preferredName} rather than for them, write them in {preferredName}'s words and share them with staff with consent, so the strategies are ones {preferredName} will actually use.
frequency: designed once and reviewed each term with the student
intensity: Student-led design with adult scribing, shared with consent
evidence_to_monitor: strategies the student chooses to use; what the student asks to change
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Provide the agreed assistance, prompting before helping
wording: The {role} should provide the agreed in-class assistance to {preferredName} under teacher and plan direction, prompting the agreed strategy before giving direct help, and recording how much prompting was needed, so support can be faded on evidence rather than habit.
frequency: in each lesson where the agreed adjustment applies
intensity: Prompt first, direct assistance only where the prompt is not enough
evidence_to_monitor: level of prompting required; tasks completed with less help than last time
linked_activities: Undertaking Tasks Independently; Listening; Interpreting Spoken Messages; Using Expressive Language: Speaking; Writing

action: Prepare adapted materials before the lesson
wording: The {role} should prepare or adapt {preferredName}'s materials in the agreed format before the lesson begins, under teacher direction, so {preferredName} starts the task at the same time as everyone else.
frequency: before each lesson where adapted materials are needed
intensity: Materials ready in advance to the agreed specification
evidence_to_monitor: lessons started on time with the right materials
linked_activities: Focusing and Directing Attention; Writing; Fine Motor Skills; Producing Non-Verbal Messages

action: Support unstructured times
wording: The {role} should be available to {preferredName} at the agreed unstructured times — recess, lunch or transitions — supporting entry into an activity or group rather than supervising from beside them, so the time is used well without creating dependence on an adult.
frequency: at the agreed break or transition times each day
intensity: Available nearby, actively supporting entry to an activity, stepping back once settled
evidence_to_monitor: activities and groups joined; time spent without adult support

action: Record observations against the plan
wording: The {role} should record short, specific observations of {preferredName} against the goals in the plan each week and give them to the teacher and the plan coordinator, so decisions are made on what is actually happening in lessons.
frequency: weekly
intensity: Brief written observations tied to the plan goals
evidence_to_monitor: observations recorded; changes made because of them

action: Support the personal care or health routine
wording: The {role}, where trained and named in the plan, should support {preferredName}'s agreed personal care or health routine at the times set out in the plan, in a private space and in a way that maintains dignity and builds whatever independence is possible, so the routine is met safely without drawing attention.
frequency: at the times set out in the plan
intensity: Trained staff only, following the documented procedure, privacy maintained
evidence_to_monitor: routine completed as planned; steps the student now manages independently
linked_activities: Looking After One’s Health; Drinking; Eating; Dressing; Toileting; Washing Oneself

action: Support excursions, camps and offsite activities
wording: The {role} should support {preferredName} on excursions, camps and offsite activities according to the risk assessment completed before the activity, so {preferredName} takes part in the same programme as everyone else.
frequency: for each offsite activity
intensity: Support level set by the risk assessment for that activity
evidence_to_monitor: offsite activities attended; supports that were needed on the day
linked_activities: Moving From Place to Place; Lifting and Carrying Objects

action: Translate the plan into subject-level adjustments
wording: The {role} should work with each subject teacher at the start of every unit to turn {preferredName}'s plan into the specific adjustments that unit needs, so the plan is applied to the actual work rather than sitting above it.
frequency: at the start of each unit in each subject
intensity: Short planning conversation per subject with agreed unit-level adjustments
evidence_to_monitor: adjustments named in unit planning; student access to the unit's tasks

action: Model the adjustment in the classroom
wording: The {role} should model or co-teach the agreed adjustment in {preferredName}'s classes at least once per teacher, then hand it back to the teacher, so staff see how it works rather than only reading about it.
frequency: at least once per teacher, and after any new adjustment is agreed
intensity: In-class modelling followed by teacher-led practice
evidence_to_monitor: teacher confidence and use after modelling

action: Check adjustments are visible in practice
wording: The {role} should check each term whether {preferredName}'s agreed adjustments are visible in classroom practice, and feed what is found back to the teacher and the plan coordinator without blame, so gaps are found by the school rather than by the family.
frequency: once a term across a sample of classes
intensity: Short classroom visits against a specific list of agreed adjustments
evidence_to_monitor: adjustments seen in practice; gaps and what was done about them

action: Arrange assessment adjustments in advance
wording: The {role} should arrange {preferredName}'s agreed assessment adjustments — such as extra time, an alternative format, a separate space or a reader or scribe — before each formal assessment, checking each one against what the task is meant to assess, so access is provided without changing what is being measured.
frequency: before each formal assessment
intensity: Arranged in advance and confirmed with the student and the teacher
evidence_to_monitor: adjustments provided and used; student report of the assessment conditions

action: Preview the week with the student
wording: The {role} should meet {preferredName} at the start of each week to preview what is coming — assessments, changes to routine, unfamiliar activities — and note anything that needs preparing, so the week holds fewer surprises.
frequency: once at the start of each week
intensity: Short individual meeting with a written or visual summary of the week
evidence_to_monitor: what the student flagged as difficult; preparation that reduced the difficulty
linked_activities: Handling Stress and Other Psychological Demands

action: Start and end of day check-in

action: Manage mid-year changes of class or subject

action: Hold the link with family and outside services

action: Debrief staff after a significant incident
wording: The {role} should debrief the staff involved after any significant incident involving {preferredName}, within the same week, covering what happened, what worked and what will change, so the response improves and staff are supported.

intensity: Plan consulted before decisions are locked in

action: Brief the year level team each term
wording: The {role} should brief the year level team on {preferredName}'s current adjustments at the start of each term, including what to do when things are not going well, so every teacher in the team is working from the same information.

action: Keep behaviour responses consistent with the plan
wording: The {role} should make sure responses to {preferredName}'s behaviour follow the agreed plan rather than the generic consequence, and check any referral against the plan before it proceeds, so the response accounts for the disability-related need.

wording: The {role} should monitor {preferredName}'s assessment load across subjects and adjust due dates where several fall in the same week, in line with the plan, so the workload is manageable without lowering what is expected.
